purpose: Corrects stored structural literals that the first-pass extractor mangled, so a validator matching on the stored string stops rejecting official NPHIES messages. Separates extractor mangling (corrections) from genuine defects in the published spec (specDefects), which are recorded, never silently fixed.
howToApply: Each correction names one artifact and every jsonPath in it whose string value equals storedLiteral. Replace the value at those paths with correctedLiteral. jsonPath is the first path; jsonPaths is the complete list. Provenance slots (source.quote, source.row, guidance, description, elementLocationRaw) are excluded by construction and must stay verbatim.

vsGate.note: The gate counted 24 RESOLVED-AFTER-NORMALISATION identifier occurrences in the SOAP samples. Two of those 24 (repositoryUniqueId, and the case-folded authorSpecialty) are spec defects, not extractor mangles, and are reclassified below. The 24 mangled $XDSDocumentEntry* literals are all present here, plus 12 more that no sample exercises and the gate therefore could not see: the two Attribute-column footnote markers on page 54788213, the FindDocuments stored-query UUID broken by an NBSP, the OID catalogue label that inherited the same NBSP, five XPaths with stray spaces that fields.json already normalises but constants.json/valuesets.json do not, and three cells holding two element paths flattened into one.

No single corrected literal is derivable, so a string patch would be a guess. The real fix is a schema change: codeSystemOid must become a list. Flagged for the valuesets owner, not patched here.

rejected.class: space present in the published spec with no derivable correction
rejected.whyRejected: page 33357874 prints the Format line as urn:ksa-ehealth:document:mappingRadio_ImagingProcedure-Modality-BodyRegion:2023 and the Example line (which is what got captured) as urn:ksa-ehealth:document: ImagingProcedure-Modality-BodyRegion:2023 — the two disagree by more than the space (mappingRadio_). No golden sample carries either. Removing the space alone would produce a literal that still does not match the Format line, so the corrected value is ambiguous. Also note the captured cell is an EXAMPLE, not a fixed value.

Confluence smart quotes (U+2018/U+2019) in XPath predicates make the stored path unparseable by any XPath engine, and fields.json preserves them in the normalised elementLocation[].path too. This is a real defect but it is uniform across hundreds of paths and is a single normalisation switch in the compiler (see extractionRule.additionalNormalisations), not a per-literal patch. Emitting hundreds of near-identical corrections would bury the 31 that matter.

source.quote / source.row / elementLocationRaw are the verbatim evidence for a rule. They MUST keep the mangled text — that is what the page actually says, and it is how a reviewer confirms the correction. Only the derived data slots are patched.

extractionRule.description:
Three independent bugs in the cell-text extractor produced every literal in `corrections`. (1) NBSP: Confluence authors press Ctrl+Shift+Space inside spans to stop identifiers wrapping, so the page carries U+00A0 MID-TOKEN ($XDSDocumentEntry\u00a0ClassCode, 14d4debf-8f97-4251-9a74\u00a0-a90016b0af0d). The extractor maps every whitespace character, NBSP included, to U+0020. NBSP must NOT be treated as whitespace inside an identifier cell: in an identifier context it is deleted, in prose it becomes a space. Verified: 0 of the 243,245 strings in spec-build still contain U+00A0, which is exactly the symptom - the information that it was an NBSP was destroyed at parse time. (2) footnotes: page 54788213 carries all 10 digit markers in the corpus. The extractor flattens the cell with a text join, so $XDSDocumentEntry ClassCode 1 becomes "$XDSDocumentEntry ClassCode 1". Strip whose text is a bare 1-2 digit run BEFORE flattening. On six rows the author typed the marker INSIDE the (CreationTimeFrom5, ServiceStartTimeTo\u00a0\u00a06, Status\u00a0\u00a03), so a second, guarded pass is needed: strip a trailing 1-2 digit run from an identifier only when the page has a numbered footnote list, the digit indexes into it, and the de-suffixed form is corroborated (a golden sample, or another row on another page). Footnotes 5 and 6 on that page literally name "CreationTimeFrom and CreationTimeTo" and "ServiceStartTimeFrom, ServiceStartTimeTo, ServiceStopTimeFrom and ServiceStopTimeTo" without digits - that is the corroboration. (3) Block-level joins:

,

and
boundaries inside one are joined with a single space, which merges two element paths into one unusable string (./extension/url= ”...” ./extension/valueReference) and leaves a space after "url=". Block boundaries must become newlines; only INLINE markup (, , , , ) is unwrapped with no separator at all. Prefer the descendant: in every identifier column on these pages the identifier is exactly the element text, and taking it first sidesteps the sibling entirely.
extractionRule.pythonSnippet:
# Drop-in replacement for the cell-text step of spec-build/_extract_lib.py. # Fixes all three defects: NBSP mid-token, footnote markers, block-level joins. import re from bs4 import BeautifulSoup, NavigableString NBSP, ZWSP, SHY = ' ', '​', '­' BLOCK = {'p', 'div', 'li', 'tr', 'br'} FOOTNOTE_SUP = re.compile(r'^\s*\d{1,2}\s*$') # an identifier: $XDSDocumentEntryClassCode, XDSDocumentEntry.eventCodeList, # authorSpecialty, urn:uuid:..., ./extension/valueReference IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r'^[$@#]?[A-Za-z_./][A-Za-z0-9_$.:/\\-]*$') def strip_footnote_sups(node): """1 next to an identifier is a footnote marker, not part of it.""" for sup in node.find_all('sup'): if FOOTNOTE_SUP.match(sup.get_text()): sup.decompose() return node def cell_text(node): """Flatten a /

/ keeping token integrity. Block boundaries -> '\n' (so a cell holding two element paths stays two lines). Inline markup -> unwrapped with NO separator (a split mid-token must not become a space). NBSP -> kept as U+00A0 here; resolved by normalise_identifier / normalise_prose, which know whether this is a token. """ out = [] def walk(n): if isinstance(n, NavigableString): out.append(str(n)) return if n.name in BLOCK and out and not out[-1].endswith('\n'): out.append('\n') for child in n.children: walk(child) if n.name in BLOCK: out.append('\n') walk(node) return ''.join(out) def normalise_prose(text): """Prose: NBSP really is a space.""" text = text.replace(ZWSP, '').replace(SHY, '').replace(NBSP, ' ') return re.sub(r'[ \t]+', ' ', text).strip() def normalise_identifier(text, page_footnotes=(), corroborate=lambda s: False): """Identifier cell: whitespace is ALWAYS an artefact, never part of the name. page_footnotes -- ordered footnote texts from the same page (may be empty) corroborate -- predicate: is this de-suffixed form attested elsewhere (an official sample, or the same row on another page)? Returns (value, flags). Never guesses silently: anything it could not resolve is returned with a flag so the row is marked low confidence. """ flags = [] raw = text.replace(ZWSP, '').replace(SHY, '').strip() squashed = re.sub(r'[\s ]+', '', raw) # delete ALL whitespace if not IDENTIFIER.match(squashed): # not a single token after all -> treat as prose, do not mangle it return normalise_prose(raw), ['not-an-identifier'] if squashed != re.sub(r'\s+', '', raw): flags.append('nbsp-removed') elif squashed != raw: flags.append('space-removed') # guarded footnote-digit strip, for markers typed inside the m = re.match(r'^(?P.*[A-Za-z])(?P\d{1,2})$', squashed) if m: stem, digits = m.group('stem'), int(m.group('digits')) if page_footnotes and 1 <= digits <= len(page_footnotes) and corroborate(stem): return stem, flags + ['footnote-digit-stripped:%d' % digits] if m.group('digits') and corroborate(stem) and not corroborate(squashed): return stem, flags + ['footnote-digit-stripped-uncorroborated:%d' % digits] flags.append('trailing-digits-kept-unverified') return squashed, flags def identifier_from_cell(td, **kw): """Preferred entry point for an identifier column. The identifier is the text where one exists; taking it first also sidesteps the sibling footnote marker entirely. """ strip_footnote_sups(td) code = td.find('code') return normalise_identifier(cell_text(code if code is not None else td), **kw) def xpath_from_cell(td): """Element-path column: also drop the spaces Confluence authors typed by hand. fields.json already does this for elementLocation[].path; constants.json and valuesets.json must call the SAME function or the two artifacts disagree. """ paths = [p for p in (l.strip() for l in cell_text(td).split('\n')) if p] fixed = [] for p in paths: p = p.replace(NBSP, ' ') p = re.sub(r'\[\s+', '[', p) # participant[ @typeCode -> participant[@typeCode p = re.sub(r'\s+\]', ']', p) p = re.sub(r'\s*/\s*', '/', p) # representedOrganization /std -> .../std fixed.append(re.sub(r'\s{2,}', ' ', p).strip()) return fixed # a list: one cell may hold several paths

additionalNormalisations.what: XPath predicates arrive with U+2018/U+2019/U+201C/U+201D (participant[@typeCode=’SBJ’]). No XPath engine accepts them.
additionalNormalisations.recommendation: map ‘’“” to ' inside element-path and predicate text only, never inside quote/guidance provenance
additionalNormalisations.notPatchedHere: uniform across hundreds of paths; one compiler switch, not per-literal patches

additionalNormalisations.what: assert that no string in any spec-build artifact matches ^\$XDS\w+\s or \s\d{1,2}$ in an identifier slot, and that identifier slots never contain U+00A0 or an internal space
additionalNormalisations.recommendation: run the assertion in the build so this class of defect cannot come back silently

extractionRule.verification: After applying every correction, all 16 identifiers the gate could only resolve after normalisation resolve EXACTLY, and 14 of the 18 corrected $XDSDocumentEntry* parameter names are literally present as rim:Slot name="..." in spec-source/golden/SOAP/ITI-18/. The remaining four ($XDSDocumentEntryEventCodeList, and the EntryType row which is additionally a spec defect) are derived from the raw HTML of page 54788213 and its footnote list.
